t.7.87.1: When that night had passed into dawn, the king, Rāghava of great splendour, having gone to the sacrificial enclosure, summoned all the ṛṣis.
t.7.87.2: Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva, Jābāli and then Kāśyapa, Viśvāmitra of long austerities, and Durvāsas of great austerities.
t.7.87.3: Then Agastya, and likewise Śakti, Bhārgava and Vāmana, the long-lived Mārkaṇḍeya, and Maudgalya of great austerities.
t.7.87.4: The Bhārgava Cyavana, Śatānanda, knower of dharma, the mighty Bharadvāja, and the radiant son of Agni.
t.7.87.5: These and many other sages of rigorous vows, and kings, tigers among men, all assembled together.
t.7.87.6: The rākṣasas of great valour and the vānaras of great strength, all those great-souled ones, came together out of curiosity.
t.7.87.7: Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas and Śūdras too, by the thousands, all assembled there to witness Sītā's oath.
t.7.87.8: Hearing that the whole assembly had gathered thus, motionless as though turned to stone, the best of sages swiftly came forward, accompanied by Sītā.
t.7.87.9: Sītā followed behind that sage, her face cast down and her palms joined, her throat choked with tears, holding Rāma within her heart.
t.7.87.10: Seeing her, Sītā, coming behind Vālmīki like Śrī following Brahmā, a great cry of “Well done!” arose.
t.7.87.11: Then a tumultuous cry of "halahalā" arose thus from all of them, their hearts agitated by a vast grief born of sorrow.
t.7.87.12: Some cried, "Well done, Sītā!" while others cried, "Well done, Rāma!" And still others there exclaimed, "Well done, well done!" to both of them alike.
t.7.87.13: Then Vālmīki, the foremost of sages, accompanied by Sītā, entered into the midst of the throngs of people and spoke thus to Rāghava.
t.7.87.14: O son of Daśaratha, this is Sītā, firm in her vows and devoted to dharma, sinless, who was abandoned by you near my hermitage.
t.7.87.15: O Rāma of great vows, Sītā will give proof to you who fear the censure of the people; you should grant her leave.
t.7.87.16: And these two sons of Jānakī, both born as twins, are your very own sons, invincible; this is the truth I tell you.
t.7.87.17: I am the tenth son of Pracetas, O delight of the Rāghavas, and I do not recall ever having spoken an untrue word; so too, these two are truly your sons.
t.7.87.18: For many thousands of years I have practised austerities; may I enjoy their fruit only as surely as Maithilī is sinless.
t.7.87.19: O Rāghava, having reflected upon the five elements with the mind as the sixth and concluded that Sītā is pure, I received her at the forest waterfall.
t.7.87.20: This woman, pure in conduct, sinless, who holds her husband as her deity, will give proof to you, who fear the censure of the people.
